subject: civics
question_text: You have probably noticed that people in Kalpattu are engaged in a variety of non-farm work. List five of these.
answer_text: Five non-farm work of people in Kalpattu village: (i) Making baskets, utensils, pots, bricks, bullock-carts etc. (ii) Blacksmiths (iii) Nursing (iv) Teaching (v) Shop-keeping (vi) Trading
final_answer: The non-farm works include making baskets, blacksmithing, nursing, teaching, and shop-keeping.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of information from the text.

subject: civics
question_text: List the different types of people you read about in Kalpattu who depend on farming. Who is the poorest among them and why?
answer_text: Different types of people who depend on farming are: (i) Big landowner (ii) Small landowners or Farmers (iii) Landless farmers or Labourers. Landless farmers or labourers are the poorest among them because they have seasonal earning.
final_answer: Landless farmers are the poorest because they have seasonal earnings and lack a fixed income.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of social structure and economic conditions.

subject: civics
question_text: Imagine you are a member of a fishing family and you are discussing whether to take a loan from the bank for an engine. What would you say?
answer_text: If I were a member of a fishing family, I would say that taking a loan from the bank for an engine is a good idea to improve and invest in the growth of the business. The engine is costly, but the bank is a trusted institution with fixed terms and rates, and buying an engine will increase income.
final_answer: Taking a loan for an engine is beneficial for improving the fishing business.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires reasoning about financial decisions and business growth.

subject: civics
question_text: Poor rural labourers like Thulasi often do not have access to good medical facilities, good schools, and other resources. You have read about inequality in the first unit of this text. The difference between her and Ramalingam is one of inequality. Do you think this is a fair situation? What do you think can be done? Discuss in class.
answer_text: The situation is not fair as the constitution of India grants equality in access to facilities. The government should ensure basic facilities for every citizen, provide loans for work, farming land, low-cost fertilizers, and set up hospitals to help them.
final_answer: The government must ensure basic facilities and support for all citizens to address inequality.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of social justice and government responsibilities.

subject: civics
question_text: What do you think the government can do to help farmers like Sekar when they get into debt? Discuss.
answer_text: The government can help farmers like Sekar by providing easy farming loans at low interest rates, insurance for their cultivation, subsidized fertilizers, pesticides, and HYV seeds, and offering farming schools and assistance at no cost.
final_answer: Government support through loans, insurance, and subsidies can help farmers manage debt.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of agricultural support systems.
